pure-announcement.rationale: Although Sweeper is the author's own tool, the post is a measured case study (842 errors, 99 files, linked PRs, an unexpected type-cascade failure) whose architectural lessons transfer beyond the product, not a launch notice.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts cover parallel fan-out orchestration, escalation ladders, or cross-run observational memory; proxy-boundary-session-capture only covers the Tapes recording layer this note builds on.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The central claims are backed by linked public PRs (#1741, #1745), the open-source repo, and concrete run metrics a reader can check or reproduce.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing claims — parallelism, not context size, is the right scaling axis for multi-file work; retries should escalate strategy rather than repeat; per-file isolation trades away cross-file type safety — are mechanisms and trade-offs that hold regardless of the tool or the 1M-context news peg.

actionability.rationale: The patterns are directly buildable without Sweeper: group issues per file, keep the orchestrator free of source code, run stateless one-file agents, escalate standard-to-retry-to-exploration with a stale threshold, and record per-round strategy outcomes for the next run.

atomicity.rationale: The note bundles at least three separable stand-alone ideas — parallel fan-out beats bigger context windows, an escalation ladder for stalled fixes, and observational memory across runs (plus the type-cascade isolation trade-off) — each of which could be its own concept, so the split is the finding.
